chunks: "Horses were wild in the lands of the Arabs, and Ibrahim and Isma'il عليهما السلام ascended Abu Qubays and called out: 'Come! Come forward!' Then no horse remained except that it yielded its reins and allowed access to its forelock."

key_terms.أَبِي قُبَيْسٍ: Abi Qubays, the mountain mentioned in the report
key_terms.نَاصِيَتِهِ: its forelock, indicating being brought under control

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith describe the taming of horses in the time of Ibrahim and Isma'il عليهما السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that horses were once wild in Arabia until Ibrahim and Isma'il عليهما السلام called them, whereupon they became submissive. It presents a historical narrative connected to the prophets and highlights a special event associated with their authority and blessed station.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2464 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Horses were once wild in the lands of the Arabs. Ibrahim (as) and Isma‘il (as) ascended Mount Abi Qubays and called out: 'Come! Come forward!'
No horse remained except that it came forward, offering its reins and submitting its forelock."
